title: ～みたいに — “like ～” (before a verb or adjective)
summary: みたいに comes before a verb or adjective and means “in the way that ～, like ～.” It is the casual counterpart of ～のように and compares an action or a state to something else.

patterns.form: 名詞 ＋ みたいに ＋ 動詞・形容詞
patterns.gloss: 鳥みたいに飛ぶ / 真夏みたいに暑い

patterns.form: 普通形 ＋ みたいに ＋ 動詞
patterns.gloss: 知っているみたいに話す (speak as if you knew)

body.p: It is the adverbial form of みたいだ: だ becomes に and describes the following verb or adjective. It means the same as 鳥のように, but is more casual and spoken.
Use it for wishes, impressions and comparisons: 鳥みたいに空を飛びたい, 子どもみたいに大きな声で笑った, 今日は真夏みたいに暑い.
Use みたいだ at the end of a sentence, みたいな before a noun, and みたいに before a verb or adjective. ～みたいになる means “turn into something like ～” and shows change.

examples.ja: 鳥（とり）みたいに空（そら）を飛（と）びたい。
examples.romaji: Tori mitai ni sora o tobitai.
examples.tr: I want to fly in the sky like a bird.

examples.ja: 子（こ）どもみたいに大（おお）きな声（こえ）で笑（わら）った。
examples.romaji: Kodomo mitai ni ōkina koe de waratta.
examples.tr: I laughed in a loud voice like a child.

examples.ja: 今日（きょう）は真夏（まなつ）みたいに暑（あつ）い。
examples.romaji: Kyō wa manatsu mitai ni atsui.
examples.tr: Today it is hot like midsummer.

pitfalls: Use みたいに before verbs and adjectives, and みたいな before nouns (鳥みたいに飛ぶ / 鳥みたいな人).
鳥のみたいに is wrong; attach it directly to the noun.
